**Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah al-Masad**

It is a Meccan surah, by consensus (ijma').

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he.﴾ ﴿His wealth and what he earned will not avail him.﴾ ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame.﴾ ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood,﴾ ﴿with a rope of twisted fiber around her neck.﴾

It has been related in a hadith that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received the revelation ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214], he said: "O Safiyya bint 'Abd al-Muttalib, O Fatima bint Muhammad, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me for whatever you wish from my wealth." Then he climbed al-Safa and called out to the clans of Quraysh: "O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so." It is also related that he shouted at the top of his voice, "Ya sabahah!" (an alarm cry), and they gathered to him from every direction. He said to them: "Tell me, if I told you that horsemen were about to attack you at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perish you today! Is for this you gathered us?" They dispersed from him, and the surah was revealed.

"Tabbat" means "she was lost" (or "ruined"). Tabab means loss and destruction. It is attributed to the two hands because the hand is the place of earning, gain, and taking hold of what one possesses. Then Allah the Exalted made it obligatory upon him that he had perished, meaning (p. 707) that this was decreed against him. In the recitation of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he has perished." Abu Lahab is 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, the paternal uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, but wretchedness had preceded him (in decree). Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin read "Abi Lahb" with a sukun on the ha'; the rest read it with a vowel on the ha'. They did not differ on its fatha in "dhati lahab."

It may also be an interrogative "ma" in the sense of affirmation, meaning: where is the benefit of his wealth and his earnings? "What he earned" may refer to worldly goods such as property and the like, or the statement may indicate that he labored in earning, and it did not come to him effortlessly, neither through inheritance nor gift or the like. Many exegetes said: what is meant by "what he earned" is his sons. It is as if He said: "His wealth and his children did not avail him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said: "The best of what a man earns is from the work of his hands, and a man's child is part of his earnings." It is related that the sons of Abu Lahab disputed before Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and they quarreled and pushed one another. Ibn 'Abbas rose to separate them, but one of them pushed him so that he fell onto his bed. He had lost his sight, so he became angry and shouted: "Remove from me this wicked earning!"
